historical_significance: Honda's first automotive engines - established the company as a car manufacturer

e_as250.notes: Honda's first production automobile engine - 4-carb mini truck engine

e_as500.notes: Chain-driven DOHC - revolutionary for its time. Derived from racing motorcycle technology

e_as600.notes: 4 Keihin carburetors, roller bearing crankshaft from motorcycle heritage

e_as800.notes: Final evolution of S-series sports car engines. Export model had 9500 rpm redline

e_n360.notes: Air-cooled engine derived from motorcycle. Extremely high-revving for its displacement

e_n600.notes: Air-cooled twin. Honda's first car sold in the USA (1970)

e_eb1.notes: Water-cooled engine that would evolve into the famous EB series

base_specifications.cooling: Varies by model (air-cooled for N-series, water-cooled for S/EB series)

notes.heritage: Honda's motorcycle racing expertise directly influenced these engines. High-revving, lightweight designs.
innovations: First Japanese car with DOHC engine (S500)
Roller bearing crankshafts from motorcycle technology
4 valves per cylinder before it was common
Extremely high specific output for the era
common_issues: Carburetor synchronization critical for multi-carb setups
notes.collectors_notes: S500/S600/S800 engines are highly prized by collectors. Complete rebuilds require specialist knowledge.
